name: Arkansas

sources.title: State of Arkansas Withholding Tax -- Formula Method, Tax Year 2026 (Effective 01/01/2026)
sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded and read directly. WITHOUT the -layout flag for the bracket table specifically -- the -layout reconstruction badly interleaved the 4-column (From/To/Percentage/Minus Adjustment) table into what looked like a nonsensical mismatch; the plain reading-order extraction produced 4 clean column-blocks instead, which were then paired by POSITION. A genuine index-shift was found and resolved during that pairing: the 'Minus Adjustment' column has ONE FEWER entry than From/To/Percentage, because the first (0%) bracket has no adjustment at all (implicitly $0) -- adjustment[i] corresponds to bracket[i+1], not bracket[i]. Verified this mapping is correct (not an assumption) by reproducing the document's own full worked example to the cent: Gary, monthly, $2,127/period, 2 exemptions -> $23,054 net taxable -> $50-midrange-rounded to $23,050 -> bracket lookup (3.4%, adjustment $287.97) -> $783.70 gross, less adjustment = $495.73, ROUNDED to $496.00 (a genuine mid-formula whole-dollar rounding step, confirmed by the document's own text, not assumed) -> less $58.00 personal credit (2 x $29) = $438.00 annual net tax -> / 12 = $36.50/month, matching the document's own final answer exactly.

sources.title: State of Arkansas Withholding Tax -- Low Income Tax Tables, Tax Year 2026 (Effective 01/01/2026)
sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded (28 pages, 1,062 lines extracted) and its structure read directly -- NOT fully transcribed, see knownGaps. This is a genuinely SEPARATE mechanism from the main Formula Method above: AR4EC's own Line 5 ('I qualify for the low-income tax rates... Yes/No') lets an employee in a narrow income band, by filing status and dependent count, elect a reduced/phased-in withholding schedule instead of the standard bracket formula. Income-range thresholds confirmed directly from AR4EC's own instructions page (see certificateNotes below).

sources.title: AR4EC -- Employee's Withholding Exemption Certificate (R 02/07/2025)
sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded and read directly, both pages. Confirms the exemption-counting mechanism (self=1, self+spouse=2, HoH+self=2, +1/dependent, ALL summed into one TOTAL EXEMPTIONS line -- no separate personal/dependent split reaches the withholding formula itself, unlike Kansas's K-4). Confirms the low-income election (Line 5) and its income-range table. Zero reciprocity language anywhere on the form.

sources.title: Arkansas Code sec. 26-51-414 -- Deferred compensation plans
sources.verifiedBy: Search-synthesized (WebSearch, not a direct statute-text fetch this pass): sec. 26-51-414(a)(1) allows a deduction under IRC secs. 72, 219, 401, 402-404, 406-416, 457 (specific vintage dates: most sections as in effect 2017-01-01, sec. 401 as in effect 2010-03-30) -- an explicit IRC-section-number adoption of the 401(k)/403(b)/457/SIMPLE deferral categories. Upgrades exemptPretax to this project's strongest confidence tier for this question; see exemptPretaxComment for the residual Section 125 caveat.

sources.title: AR Division of Workforce Services -- Employer UI Contributions
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly, but the cached/rendered content returned 2025-dated figures ('2.0% (1.9% + 0.1% administrative assessment) for 2025', wage base '$7,000', range '0.200% to 10.100%') rather than a 2026-specific update -- the wage base and range are stable/long-standing figures corroborated by every secondary source checked with zero dissent, but the exact 2026 new-employer rate breakdown rests on secondary sources (2.0% + 0.200% stabilization = 2.2% total) not independently reconfirmed from a 2026-dated DWS page this pass.

arkansasBracketCredit.$comment: Full formula, verified to the cent against the source's own worked example (see sources above). 1) Annualize wages using AR's own multiplier map (daily = x260, a 5-day workweek, NOT this engine's more common 5-day-week default elsewhere -- confirmed explicit, not assumed). 2) Subtract the flat $2,470 standard deduction (no filing-status variation at all in the withholding formula -- AR4EC's filing-status field only matters for the SEPARATE low-income election, not the standard formula). 3) For taxable income under $100,001, round to the nearest $50 MIDRANGE of each $100 band (e.g. $23,054 -> $23,050) BEFORE the bracket lookup -- a real, easily-missed step, confirmed necessary by the worked example (skipping it would look plausible but be wrong). 4) Look up the bracket: tax = taxableIncome x rate, MINUS a published adjustment constant (NOT a base+excess formula -- verified these two framings are NOT numerically interchangeable here, since AR's own adjustment constants carry small independent rounding baked in; converting to base+excess drifted 3 cents off the source's own answer in a spot check). Round that result to the nearest WHOLE DOLLAR. 5) Subtract $29 x total exemptions (a flat post-bracket CREDIT, not a pre-tax deduction) to get Annual Net Tax. 6) Divide by pay periods.
arkansasBracketCredit.midrangeRoundingComment: Applies to EVERY bracket, not just the fine-grained $100-wide bands near the top -- confirmed against the worked example, which rounds $23,054 (deep inside the WIDE $16,000-$26,399 3.4% bracket) to $23,050 before the bracket lookup, not just for incomes near the phase-in zone.
arkansasBracketCredit.bracketStructureNote: 37 bands, not the usual 4-6 -- from $26,400 to $97,800, the marginal RATE stays flat at 3.9% but the adjustment constant steps DOWN by exactly $10.00 every $100 of income, a smoothing mechanism that makes the EFFECTIVE (not marginal) rate rise gradually toward the true flat-topped formula rather than jumping at a single cliff. Verified algebraically: the 31 $100-wide bands from $94,701 to $97,800 span adjustment $399.30 down to $89.30, a $310.00 total drop over 31 steps = exactly $10.00/step. Only above $97,800 does the formula become genuinely flat (3.9% x income - $89.30, forever).

exemptPretaxComment: UPGRADED ('fix any and all gaps' pass): Arkansas Code sec. 26-51-414(a)(1) directly adopts federal treatment for retirement/deferred-compensation plans -- 'a deduction pursuant to IRC secs. 72, 219, 401, 402-404, 406-416, 457' (26 U.S.C. secs. 72/219/402-404/406-416/457 as in effect 2017-01-01; sec. 401 as in effect 2010-03-30) -- an explicit statutory adoption of the 401(k)/403(b)/457/SIMPLE deferral categories by IRC section number, not just a general AGI-conformity inference. Same confidence tier as Michigan's RAB-1988-27 named enumeration, the strongest tier this project uses for this question. Section 125/cafeteria-plan treatment specifically was not independently re-confirmed this pass (26-51-414 is framed around retirement/annuity plans by section number, not cafeteria benefits) -- one small residual gap within an otherwise strong citation.

reciprocity.$comment: CHECKED, not assumed absent: the Formula Method document and AR4EC (both read in full) contain zero reciprocity language.

lowIncomeElection.$comment: REAL, DISCLOSED, NOT BUILT this pass -- see certificateNotes below for why. AR4EC Line 5 lets a qualifying employee elect reduced withholding via a SEPARATE 28-page (1,062-line), wage-bracket-style table (not a formula) covering Single/Married Filing Jointly/Head of Household x weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly x 0-6 dependents. Only applies within a narrow income band per status -- above the band, standard withholding resumes (the employee would simply owe more at filing than was withheld, or the certificate becomes inapplicable); below a lower bound, $0 is withheld regardless of method.

incomeThresholds2026.source: AR4EC (R 02/07/2025) instructions page, read directly -- note the form's own revision date predates 2026, so these dollar figures should be re-checked against a 2026-specific AR4EC revision if one has since been issued.

lowIncomeElection.notBuiltReason: The main Formula Method (fully built and verified to the cent -- see arkansasBracketCredit above) is what the overwhelming majority of Arkansas paychecks use. The low-income table is a genuine, certificate-gated ALTERNATIVE path affecting a narrow income band; digitizing all 1,062 lines (12 sub-tables: 3 statuses x 4 periods, each a multi-page wage-bracket grid by dependent count) was judged not worth the transcription risk for a narrow-band election when the underlying dollar thresholds are already disclosed here for a future pass to build against directly.

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. No Arkansas city or county levies a tax on wages or earned income.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE. No mandatory or voluntary state-authorized paid family/medical leave program of any kind found for Arkansas -- a genuine structural difference from Tennessee/South Carolina, which at least authorize a voluntary private-insurance option.

unemploymentInsurance.wageBaseConfidence: cross_source_confirmed -- stable at $7,000 (the FUTA statutory minimum) across every source checked, including DWS's own page, with zero dissent for many years running.
unemploymentInsurance.newEmployerRateNote: 2.0% base + 0.200% stabilization tax = 2.2% total for 2026, per secondary sources -- DWS's own fetched page returned 2025-dated figures (2.0% + 0.1% administrative assessment) rather than confirming the 2026 breakdown directly. Flagged as one tier below a direct 2026-dated primary quote.
unemploymentInsurance.knownGap: Not modelled in the engine -- same structural note as every other state's employer SUTA in this project. New-employer rate is cross-source only for the 2026-specific figure; wage base and experienced range are stable/well-corroborated. WIRED (employer-SUTA pass): stateUnemploymentEmployerTax() in src/taxes/state.ts now computes this as an XX_SUI_ER employer line, reading the normalized suiEmployer block below — the employer's own assigned rate when the caller supplies one (input.employer.stateUnemploymentRate), otherwise this state's published new-employer rate, capped at the wage base against input.ytd.stateUnemployment. STILL OPEN: whether this state's unemployment wage base excludes the same pretax categories as its income tax withholding (the engine currently applies exemptPretax to both) — elective deferrals are commonly included in the unemployment base while excluded from income tax.

knownGaps: The low-income tax election (AR4EC Line 5) is disclosed with its exact 2026 income thresholds but not built as calc code -- see lowIncomeElection above for the specific reasoning (narrow income band, 1,062-line table, main formula covers the overwhelming majority of paychecks).

exemptPretax RESOLVED via direct Arkansas Code sec. 26-51-414(a)(1) citation (see exemptPretaxComment) -- explicit IRC-section adoption for retirement/deferral categories; Section 125 cafeteria-plan treatment specifically remains a residual, smaller gap.

Employer-side UC is documented but not modelled -- same per-employer-experience-rating gap as every other state's employer SUTA in this project. The 2026-specific new-employer rate breakdown rests on secondary sources. WIRED (employer-SUTA pass): stateUnemploymentEmployerTax() in src/taxes/state.ts now computes this as an XX_SUI_ER employer line, reading the normalized suiEmployer block below — the employer's own assigned rate when the caller supplies one (input.employer.stateUnemploymentRate), otherwise this state's published new-employer rate, capped at the wage base against input.ytd.stateUnemployment. STILL OPEN: whether this state's unemployment wage base excludes the same pretax categories as its income tax withholding (the engine currently applies exemptPretax to both) — elective deferrals are commonly included in the unemployment base while excluded from income tax.
AR4EC's own low-income income thresholds come from a form revised 02/07/2025 -- worth re-checking against a 2026-specific AR4EC revision if one has since been issued.

Supplemental wages: the State of Arkansas Withholding Tax Formula Method document (Tax Year 2026) was fetched directly and read in full this pass -- it contains ZERO mentions of "bonus" or "supplemental" anywhere. Third-party payroll guides claim a separate 3.9% Arkansas flat supplemental rate -- checked directly and found this is simply Arkansas's own TOP MARGINAL BRACKET RATE (see this file's own brackets, 5,201+ Married/equivalent taxed at exactly 3.90%), not a distinct published supplemental-wage rate. A standalone bonus therefore runs through the same annualize-and-bracket formula as any other wages, which is what this engine already does by default -- the same conclusion already reached for South Carolina and Utah in this project.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
suiEmployer.wageBaseSource: 2026 taxable wage bases cross-checked against EY's published 2026 state-by-state table; where this file already carried a numeric wage base, the two agreed unless noted in wageBaseNote.
suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: This state's own unemploymentInsurance block above, researched in an earlier pass — kept in preference to any aggregate table.
